question: M04: port J10-I to cosmography -- the redshift-dependent a0-radius test of the BLR transfer-function atom+lag pair.

checks.name: C1 a0(z) = a0(0)[u(0)/u(z)]^2 inverts G237's u-law exactly
checks.measured: max rel err = 3.33e-16 over 3 laws x 6 z
checks.reading: Algebraic inversion of u(z) = u(0)[a0(0)/a0(z)]^{1/2}. Verified on framework/M-RISE/(1+z)^{3/2}.

checks.name: C2 r_B(z)/r_B(0) = [a0(0)/a0(z)]^{1/2}; framework z-invariant
checks.reading: The BLR a0-radius inherits G237's u(z) law 1:1; the z-ratio is the density-local radius's ONLY z-content and is scale-free.

checks.name: C2b deep-MOND r_M(1e9 Msun) is the kpc-scale contrast, not r_B
checks.measured: r_M = 1.454e+06 ld (~1.22 kpc) vs density-local r_B(0) = 40.9 ld
checks.reading: J10's density-local reading (a0(rho_B) >> a0) is the BLR radius; the z-law applies to the density-local radius via S3-05's a0(z) factor.

checks.name: C3 J10-I(z) identity holds at every z (1e-12)
checks.reading: J10-I(z) = -lnA r_B(z)/(c d_phys) == (r_B(z)/R(z)) W(q), tau0-free (cancellation genuine, K01 GO).

checks.name: C4 atom z-invariance (rest-frame opacity) + window z-invariance
checks.reading: tau0, q are rest-frame (opacity is rest-frame: differential depth and source geometry do not redshift); observed NOVA/time axes must be rest-frame-corrected (C7). The mock carries this exactly.

checks.name: C5 pair (A(z1), d_phys(z1)) inverts to (tau0, q) = (2, 1) exactly
checks.reading: q = (1-W/2)/(W/4-1/3), tau0 = -lnA/(1+q/3); the pair at ONE redshift fixes the transfer function (K04 inversion, this port: restricted to the window observable).

checks.name: C6 closed-form chain predicts the lag ratio at z2 (noiseless, 5 SE kill bound)
checks.reading: d(z2)/d(z1) = [a0(z1)/a0(z2)]^{1/2}: E[D] cancels (transfer-function observables drop out), M_b cancels; the lag ratio is a pure a0-cosmography number. Shown (tau0,q)-independent. The registered self-kill: failure at >5 SE here means the port is wrong.

checks.name: C7 observer-frame lags need the /(1+z) correction (else phantom kill)
checks.measured: naive obs-frame ratio 2.3078 -> J10-I_naive(z=2) = 0.7704 < 4/3 (PHANTOM violation); rest-frame ratio 1.0000255012 -> J10-I = 1.777778 (open)
checks.reading: d_phys(obs) = (1+z) d_phys(rest); the z-test must use rest-frame lags d_obs/(1+z), else a growing (1+z2)/(1+z1) factor mimics a shrinking-radius rival on the wrong side.

checks.name: C8 framework z-curve flat at W(q), OPEN at every z<3 with 3-sigma band
checks.reading: When the true BLR radius obeys the a0(z) law, J10-I(z) = W(q) at EVERY z: the window can never close (prediction: flatness).

checks.name: C9 M-RISE world: window CLOSES high; z_c(1) = 0.156 (bisection)
checks.reading: True radius obeying a growing-a0 rival gives a too-short lag at the framework radius -> J10-I(z) = W(q).sqrt(a0_rival/a0_fw) EXITS ABOVE 2.0. The 3-sigma-violated exit z follows (C10).

checks.name: C10 at z=1 the rival deviates 24.0 d ~ 11 sigma (S/N=30); 3-sigma needs ~6.1-6.6 d
checks.measured: d_fw(1) = 61.351 d, d_MRISE(1) = 37.348 d, dev = 24.00 d; sigma(d) = 2.045 d -> lag-only z = +11.7, 3-sigma floor 6.14 d (atom-incl 6.55 d); window z-stat at z=1 = +8.9; 3-sigma WINDOW violation from z = 0.345
checks.reading: Per-object S/N=30 (L05 JWST design lane IN FLIGHT -> assumed, stated in md) in atom and lag: se(d)/d = 1/30; K09 derivative se(J10-I)/J10-I = sqrt((se(A)/(A|lnA|))^2 + (se(d)/d)^2) = 3.56%. The rival sits +11.7 sigma (lag) / +8.9 sigma (window incl. atom noise) at z=1 -- ONE object resolves it.

checks.name: C11 ratio-chain falsifier: M-RISE excluded at 3 sigma from z2 ~ 0.62
checks.measured: M-RISE z-stats at z2 = 0.5/1/2: ['-2.05', '-5.35', '-8.78'] (SE = 0.0471); 3-sigma exclusion from z2 = 0.617; framework-world noiseless residuals ['-2.2e-16', '-2.2e-16', '-2.2e-16']
checks.reading: The a0-law prediction d(z2)/d(z1) = [a0(z1)/a0(z2)]^{1/2} with SE = sqrt(2)/S/N per pair: a rival world is excluded at 3 sigma by one pair beyond z2 ~ 0.6, at 5 sigma beyond ~0.85; the framework world's own residuals are zero to float precision.

checks.name: C12 S/N=30 draws: (tau0,q) recovered; M-RISE single-pair 3-sigma violations >= 90% at z=0.5
checks.measured: q_rec = 1.046 +/- 0.452 (truth 1), tau0_rec = 2.001 (truth 2); M-RISE z2=0.5 single-pair 3-sigma violation rate 98.5%
checks.reading: Seeded draws, per-object S/N=30 in atom and lag. Framework world recovers the transfer function; M-RISE world trips the window on a single object pair from z=0.5 on.

checks.name: C13 pre-registered self-check: chain closure <= 5 SE (port not wrong)
checks.reading: Kill condition from the task: if the closed-form chain fails its own synthetic check at >5 SE the port is wrong and must be reported honestly. Measured closure is float-level; the port is self-consistent.

z_curve: framework world: J10-I(z) = 1.777778 FLAT at every z<3 (window OPEN; band [1.589, 1.968] at 3-sigma, S/N=30, inside [4/3,2]); M-RISE world: J10-I = 2.184, 2.418, 2.920, 3.728 at z = 0.3/0.5/1/2 -> CLOSED high from z_c = 0.156 (q=1; q=0: 0.000, q=3: 0.331, q=10: 0.540); 3-sigma window violation from z = 0.345; chain excludes a growing-a0 world at 3 sigma from z2 = 0.617; at z=1 the rival sits +8.9 sigma above the window edge (dev 24.0 d vs 3-sigma 6.1-6.6 d).
verdict: J10-I(z) ported to cosmography: under the framework's a0(z) law (G237 S3-05) the BLR radius obeys r_B(z) = r_B(0)[a0(0)/a0(z)]^{1/2} and J10-I(z) = W(q) is FLAT -- window OPEN at every z<3, prediction = the atom+lag pair is z-invariant at rest-frame precision. The measured (A, d_phys) pair at two redshifts inverts to (tau0, q) once (recovered 2.000/1.000 to 1e-10) and predicts the lag ratio [a0(z1)/a0(z2)]^{1/2} (E[D]- and M_b-free), verified on synthetic inputs at 1e-13 (5-SE self-kill bound 5e-6: PASS). A growing-a0 rival (M-RISE) closes the window high at z_c ~ 0.156 (q=1) and is excluded at 3 sigma from z ~ 0.35 (window) / z2 ~ 0.62 (chain); one S/N=30 object at z=1 resolves it at ~11 sigma (24 d vs 6.1-6.6 d floor). Falsifier registered: any BLR scatter-lag pair whose J10-I(z) violates the a0(z)-law window at >=3 sigma kills the framework radius law at the COSMOGRAPHIC level. Synthetic data only; no git commit.
